source.title: Weakly Supervised Vision-and-Language Pre-training with Relative Representations
source.authors: Chi Chen; Peng Li; Maosong Sun; Yang Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether image and text can be aligned using a shared relative-representation space, and whether the measured quality depends on anchor choices. It does not test convergence as models scale.
record.gate_note: The paper measures weakly aligned data quality using CLIPScore, and varies the number and selection method of anchors. Its downstream task tables compare pre-training recipes, but those task scores do not directly measure representation convergence or mapping loss and are not included as rows. Figure 3 gives anchor-count curves without exact values; the paper describes the trend in text.
record.test_reason: The paper takes relative representations as a tool for weakly supervised vision-language pre-training. It relies on Moschella et al.'s claim that relative representations from different models are similar. It does not test that claim. Its numbers are the quality of its own retrieved or generated image-text pairs (CLIPScore) against a tag-based baseline, and that quality as anchor count and selection vary. They show how well the method performs, not how aligned or interchangeable independent models' representations are. No model scale, quality sweep, seeds, features or similarity-metric comparison is studied.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that relative representations bridge image and text for weakly supervised pre-training, giving better weakly aligned data and state-of-the-art results over tag-based methods. In the Limitations section they say the effects of other encoders and anchor sources, standard VLP, and other modalities remain unexplored.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cosine similarities to a small set of paired cross-modal anchors to create relative representations, retrieve or generate weakly aligned pairs, and train a vision-language model; it does not test model convergence across scale.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieved-data quality improves with more anchors; anchor selection matters, with diverse sampling generally better and non-diverse sampling producing much lower scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-modal retrieval via relative representations from independently trained unimodal encoders (ViT, Sentence-BERT) beats tag retrieval (CLIPScore 63.31 vs 57.94). On COCO it stays well below ground-truth pairs (about 0.67–0.69 vs 0.79 in Figure 3). Quality rises with anchor count, and non-diverse anchors collapse it to about 39–41.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative representations built from a few thousand paired anchors allow partial, anchor-dependent cross-modal matching between independently trained unimodal encoders.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper does not test convergence across model scale or capability. Figure 3's exact plotted values are not reported in the text, and Table 6 does not name its data-quality metric. The authors also state that they do not fully explore effects of different unimodal encoders or anchor sources.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream task results in Tables 1-4 and Figures 4 are excluded because they report task performance rather than representation alignment or mapping quality.

untested.parts: All of it: no comparison across model scale or capability.
No sweep of vision or language encoder quality.
No models trained from different seeds.
It uses relative representations between ViT and Sentence-BERT but does not measure mapping loss against original or paired representations. No linear maps or stitching.
No comparison of similarity metrics or out-of-distribution inputs for a convergence measure. Anchor sensitivity is reported only as a method hyperparameter.
No plateau or analysis of causes.

missing.what: Ground-truth pair CLIPScore (~0.79) and tag-retrieval curve plotted alongside Relrep in Figure 3; this is the only comparator showing the gap to true alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's rating of 'tests' (T2), with supports labels for V4 and V6, is overturned. The rows compare the study's own data-construction method with a tag baseline, and anchor settings are method hyperparameters. Neither measures representation convergence or mapping loss between models. The convergence premise is assumed from Moschella et al. (2022). Table 6's metric is unnamed but is likely CLIPScore×100.

versions.untested_parts: Model scale, capability, independent training, and convergence across architectures, objectives, or data.
No sweep of vision and language model quality or test of whether their alignment rises as both improve.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations.
Tests relative representations for image-text matching, but not the amount of loss relative to original representations, linear mapping, stitching, or mapping without paired anchors.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are examined.
Varies anchor count and anchor selection, but does not compare alternative similarity metrics or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, or whether alignment plateaus.

rows.subject: Retrv (Tag)
rows.operation_detail: Measured weakly-aligned image-text data quality with CLIPScore
rows.note: Tag-based retrieval comparator for relative-representation retrieval.
rows.check: Tag-based retrieval baseline for the study's own data-construction method (Table 5). This is method comparison, not a measure of representation convergence or mapping loss.

rows.subject: Retrv (Relrep)
rows.operation_detail: Measured weakly-aligned image-text data quality with CLIPScore
rows.note: The authors describe relative-representation retrieval as having significantly higher data quality than tag-based retrieval.
rows.check: CLIPScore of the study's own relative-representation retrieval (63.31) against the tag baseline (57.94). This compares the method with another method. There is no ground-truth or original-space comparator in Table 5, so mapping loss can't be read.

rows.subject: Retrv (Relrep) + Rel2Cap
rows.operation_detail: Measured weakly-aligned image-text data quality after retrieval and pseudo-caption generation
rows.note: The result includes Rel2Cap pseudo-caption generation in addition to relative-representation retrieval.
rows.check: Adds the Rel2Cap generator. This is the performance of the study's own pipeline, not representation alignment.

rows.subject: Retrv (Relrep)
rows.operation_detail: Measured retrieved-data quality while varying the number of anchors
rows.note: The text says retrieved-data quality improves as anchor count increases; exact plotted score is not stated.
rows.check: Figure-only value. It is anchor-count sensitivity of the method's retrieval quality on COCO, not a convergence measure. The figure shows Relrep at roughly 0.67–0.69, well below ground-truth pairs at about 0.79.
